methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke represents community-led evaluation and deployment of AI tools outside traditional tech hubs, signaling potential for distributed deep capability if local capacity-building succeeds beyond initial assessment phase.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon scrapping four NoVA data center plans due to local backlash reveals infrastructure concentration tensions, but the repurposing decision doesn't redistribute AI capability—it simply constrains growth in the already-dominant hub.

signals.title: Data center rumors fly in Marion after town council won’t name developer interested in 200 acres of government property
signals.signal_reading: Marion data center rumors exemplify how rural areas attract infrastructure (shallow presence) without accompanying technical workforce development or local AI capability—energy consumption without empowerment.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: Governor's statewide AI cybersecurity plan suggests centralized defensive capability development likely to concentrate expertise in Richmond and NoVA rather than distribute AI security knowledge across all regions.

signals.title: Lawyers need AI education, not AI legislation - Virginia Lawyers Weekly
signals.signal_reading: Legal sector's call for AI education over legislation signals professional class recognizing need for deep fluency rather than passive tool use—if training distributes beyond metro firms, could enable peer-network learning across Virginia's legal community.
